summary.text: Vince Fong is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for California's 20th District, a Bakersfield native who worked for Reps. Bill Thomas and Kevin McCarthy before serving in the California State Assembly from 2017 to 2024. He won a May 2024 special election to succeed McCarthy and was elected to a full term that November.

paragraphs.text: Born in Bakersfield, California, in 1979. Wikipedia reports that his parents were Chinese immigrants and that he attended West High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from UCLA in 2001 and a master's degree in public administration from Princeton University in 2003.

According to his official biography, he began his career with Rep. Bill Thomas, then chair of the House Ways and Means Committee, working on international trade policy, and later spent nearly a decade as district director to Rep. Kevin McCarthy in Kern County.

His official biography says he helped organize a Valley Fever Symposium to draw national attention to the disease, and Wikipedia lists service on the boards of Goodwill Industries of South Central California, the Jim Burke Education Foundation and Honor Flight Kern County.

Elected to the California State Assembly in 2016 and re-elected in 2018, 2020 and 2022, representing Bakersfield-area districts. Bills he authored include measures on catalytic converter theft and wildfire prevention through controlled grazing; he resigned his seat on May 24, 2024.

After McCarthy resigned from Congress effective December 31, 2023, Fong ran in the special election, advanced to a runoff against Tulare County Sheriff Mike Boudreaux, and won the May 21, 2024 runoff, 60 percent to 39 percent. He was sworn in on June 3, 2024, and won a full term in November 2024.

Serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure, Science, Space, and Technology, and Homeland Security committees, and is a member of the Republican Study Committee, Western Caucus and Congressional Valley Fever Task Force, among other caucuses.
According to his official biography, he is a lifelong Kern County resident who lives in Bakersfield with his wife, Amanda.
